body:
[aida:reviewer] NOTHING TO GATE YET — and one gap between the authorisation and the
substrate that I would rather flag before work starts than after.

I CHECKED FOR THE THING I NOW GATE:

    remote branches matching 1532 / hold-kind / merge-hold   none
    local branches matching 1532                             none
    open PRs mentioning 1532                                 none
    BUG-1532 status                                          approved

So the implementation has not started or has not pushed, and there is no diff for me to
read. I will keep checking for a branch on each poll rather than waiting to be told.

THE GAP: you authorised the work verbally and the spec still reads APPROVED, not
IN PROGRESS. Nothing in the substrate says anyone is on it.

Concretely, while that holds: `aida ps` shows no session for it, `aida status` counts it
as open unstarted work, and it stays in the candidate set any drain or seat would draw
from. If the lane restarts before the spec flips, BUG-1532 is eligible for dispatch to
someone else while the product seat is mid-implementation — which is the double-dispatch
shape, on a spec whose whole subject is a guard that does not bind.

I am not asking you to change it for my benefit; I do not need the status to review the
diff. I am flagging it because the substrate-must-not-lie rule exists for the case where
a second party acts on the stale value, and with the lane stopped I am the only party
watching this spec — which makes the exposure low right now and exactly as easy to miss
when it stops being low.

It is your dispatch, so the flip is yours or the product seat's to make rather than mine.

ON c3: good, and the part I would keep is the explicit instruction not to justify it by
noisiness. The inversion only works if someone reaches for that rationale, so naming it
as a trap is what stops the next reader reconstructing it from scratch — a rationale you
have forbidden is harder to reinvent than one you merely did not write.

ON TASK-1415 c8 BEING KEPT SHORT: agreed, and the alarm-asymmetry sentence is the one to
protect if it gets trimmed further. The mechanics of checking a conversion are
recoverable by anyone who thinks about it for a minute; that an alarming wrong number
buys LESS scrutiny than a boring one is the counterintuitive half and the reason the rule
is worth having at all.
subject: Nothing to gate yet (no branch, no PR) — but BUG-1532 still reads Approved while authorised, so it stays in the candidate set any restarted lane would draw from
